title: Armenian and Azerbaijani forces clash on the border and Russia urges a halt
body:
Armenian and Azerbaijani forces exchanged fire along their shared border on Tuesday, 16 November 2021, in one of the deadliest incidents since the 2020 war. Each side blamed the other. Azerbaijan's defence ministry said seven of its service members were killed and ten wounded, while Al Jazeera's headline put the figure at eight. Armenian officials reported one casualty, said 13 soldiers had been captured and said 24 more were missing. Armenia's defence ministry said Azerbaijan's military opened fire on Armenian positions, while the Azerbaijani government accused Armenia of a large-scale provocation.

The day before the clashes, on 15 November, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan accused Azerbaijani troops of violating the border and dismissed his defence minister over the incident. Fighting stopped on the evening of 16 November and a ceasefire appeared to be holding the following day. Russian Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu telephoned his Armenian and Azerbaijani counterparts and urged them to stop fighting, and Pashinyan also spoke with President Vladimir Putin about the situation.

Armenia's Security Council called on Russia to help protect the country's territorial integrity. Russia had brokered the November 2020 agreement that ended the Nagorno-Karabakh war and had deployed almost 2,000 peacekeepers to the region.
